defects.what: The AI chat placeholder prompts input in Russian alongside Spanish and English, which creates confusion and undermines trust for an app targeted at families relocating to Spanish-speaking Latin America.
defects.evidence: Placeholder text reads: 'Type your message in Spanish, English, or Russian...'
defects.fix: Change the placeholder text to 'Type your message in Spanish or English...' to match the target audience and context.

defects.what: The plan card says 'Trial days left: 14' while the top bar says '14 days trial', contradicting the user being on day 2 and suggesting either broken tracking or an uncalibrated counter.
defects.evidence: Card displays 'Trial days left: 14' alongside an immediate prompt 'Continue for $11 a month'.
defects.fix: Accurately compute and display remaining trial days based on activation date (e.g., '12 days left').

result.best: The integrated cross-channel ecosystem that links adult practice on WhatsApp/Telegram with specific, real-world school notes and visibility into the child's classroom progress.
result.why_pay_or_not: At $11/month, having a single hub that tracks both my daughter's Spanish classroom recaps and practical parent communication tools (like school absence notes) solves a daily real-world pain point for expat parents.

defects.where: Middle column, 'Everyday life in Panama' and 'Food and the table in Panama' modules
defects.what: Modules display '0 words' despite listing lesson time and phrase counts, making lessons appear broken, empty, or unmaintained.
defects.evidence: Both cards show '0 words' alongside '8 min / 4 phrases' and '6 min / 3 phrases', unlike other beginner cards which show actual word counts.
defects.fix: Populate the actual word counts or omit the word metric entirely when 0.

defects.where: Right column, 'Video moments with EspaLuz' section
defects.what: Unclear privacy and data handling concerning personal family media uploaded for children.
defects.evidence: Text states 'choose a short clip or photo... clip stays on your device: EspaLuz looks only at 3 still pictures from it', which is technically confusing and contradictory about whether videos are uploaded, analyzed by AI, or reviewed by humans.
defects.fix: Provide explicit, parent-friendly privacy text clearly explaining whether media leaves the device, who/what analyzes it, and how child data is protected.

result.best: The 'Phrases you've collected' section linking specific, real-life WhatsApp and Telegram interactions directly to practical school and social phrases.
result.why_pay_or_not: The core WhatsApp integration is practical, but confusing media-privacy explanations and unpolished zero-word module placeholders make me hesitate to pay a recurring subscription.

defects.what: The AI bot explicitly announces itself as an Spanish and English teacher instead of Spanish and Russian, contradicting the product's core promise.
defects.evidence: Text states: '¡Привет! Я ваш двуязычный ИИ-преподаватель Начните разговор, чтобы изучать испанский и английский вместе'.
defects.fix: Change the prompt/copy to state that it teaches Spanish from Russian (e.g., 'изучать испанский на русском').

defects.what: The CTA button immediately triggers a paid subscription during an active trial without clarifying whether billing happens now or after the trial ends.
defects.evidence: Card shows 'Осталось дней пробного периода: 14' but the action button bluntly says 'Продолжить за $11 в месяц'.
defects.fix: Update button label to explicitly state trial conditions, e.g., 'Перейти на подписку за $11/мес после триала'.

result.best: Unified cross-channel tracking that aggregates family progress across WhatsApp, Telegram, web, and kids' lessons in one cohesive dashboard.
result.why_pay_or_not: The dashboard feels cluttered and contradictory (offering English practice instead of Spanish for Russian speakers), making it feel raw compared to polished solutions like ChatGPT and Duolingo.

defects.what: Translations of collected phrases are provided in English instead of Russian, alienating Russian-speaking users who may not know English.
defects.evidence: Phrases like 'Justificar la ausencia' are translated as 'To justify the absence', 'Pedir tarea' as 'To ask for homework', and 'Muchas gracias por la invitación' as 'Thank you very much for the invitation'.
defects.fix: Translate all target phrases into Russian (e.g., 'Объяснить отсутствие', 'Спросить домашнее задание') matching the user's interface language.

defects.what: The subtitle explicitly states questions have English translations, contradicting the Russian interface and confusing the user.
defects.evidence: Text states: '6 коротких вопросов на испанском, под каждым перевод на английский.'
defects.fix: Provide Russian translations under the prompts and change the note to 'под каждым перевод на русский'.

result.best: Hyper-local Panama contextualization integrated into real household routines (like school communication and walking the dog).
result.why_pay_or_not: I wouldn't pay because relying on English translations in a product marketed to Russian-speaking expats creates unnecessary friction and feels like an unpolished wrapper around generic AI prompts.

defects.where: Middle column, 'Chatea con EspaLuz' input area
defects.what: The language selector defaults to Spanish practice despite the user onboarding profile indicating native Spanish settling in and wanting English practice.
defects.evidence: Dropdown selector is explicitly set to 'es Español' with the prompt 'Inicia una conversación para practicar español e inglés juntos' instead of prioritizing English or Panama-specific local guidance.
defects.fix: Set the default chat mode to English practice (or country transition advice) automatically based on the user's selected onboarding preference.

defects.where: Right column, 'Tu primer año en Panamá' milestone list
defects.what: Panama national cultural milestones have no dates or actionable context, reading generically as 'Cuando llegue'.
defects.evidence: Items like 'Tu primer Carnaval', 'Un desfile o una banda escolar', and 'Tu primer verano' all display the placeholder tag 'Cuando llegue' instead of actual Panamanian seasonal or calendar dates (e.g., Carnaval in Feb/Mar, Verano starting mid-December).
defects.fix: Populate known seasonal and recurring Panamanian events with their actual annual calendar months or specific date ranges.

result.best: The Panama-specific integration roadmap ('Tu primer año en Panamá') covering local cultural dates like Fiestas Patrias and school band parades alongside cross-platform tracking.
result.why_pay_or_not: It feels fragmented across too many channels (web, WhatsApp, Telegram) with generic placeholders ('Cuando llegue') instead of providing dense, reliable engineering-grade relocation logistics.

defects.where: Middle column, 'Lecciones para vivir en Panamá' cards ('Saludos y cortesía en Panamá')
defects.what: The lessons treat a native Spanish speaker as a basic language learner rather than helping with cultural settling or English practice.
defects.evidence: Shows tag 'Principiante' and teaches extremely basic Spanish phrases like 'Buenos días, ¿cómo está?' and 'Por favor' to someone who stated they already speak Spanish natively.
defects.fix: Adapt lesson content based on onboarding so native Spanish speakers see local Panamanian idioms/slang and English practice instead of basic Spanish greetings.

defects.what: Roleplay feature forces Spanish speaking with English translation instead of supporting English practice as requested.
defects.evidence: Fine print specifies '6 preguntas cortas en español, con el inglés debajo de cada una. Responde con la voz o escribiendo' instead of letting the user practice speaking English.
defects.fix: Allow the user to select the conversation language so that practice matches their goal to practice English.

result.best: The Panama-specific integration concept (local context and tips tied across messaging apps like WhatsApp/Telegram).
result.why_pay_or_not: It completely ignored my setup preferences and is trying to teach basic Spanish to a native Spanish speaker instead of helping my family settle in and practice English.

defects.what: The bot addressed me by the wrong name ('Ana' instead of Jennifer).
defects.evidence: '¡Qué emocionante, Ana! 🎓 Una graduación es un momento enorme...'
defects.fix: Ensure the user profile name ('Jennifer') is correctly referenced and not hardcoded or hallucinated as 'Ana'.

defects.what: Internal technical markup was leaked directly into the chat interface.
defects.evidence: '[VIDEO SCRIPT END] Sofi aprendió "escuela" y "maestra"... [VIDEO SCRIPT END]'
defects.fix: Strip internal prompts, delimiters, and system script tags before outputting the response to the user.

result.best: The practical, localized guidance for the CSS clinic visit, including exact paperwork, arrival tips for Panama's weather, and the exact phonetic Spanish phrase to use at the window.
result.why_pay_or_not: Calling me the wrong name and leaking technical script tags into the conversation makes the product feel sloppy and unvetted, which breaks trust for a paid service.

defects.what: The system calls the user by the wrong name, breaking trust immediately.
defects.evidence: ESPALUZ writes: '¡Qué emocionante, Ana! 🎓' when answering me (Marina).
defects.fix: Ensure the system pulls the correct user profile name rather than hardcoded or cross-contaminated user data.

defects.what: Raw internal video prompt markers leaked directly into the chat response, making the app look unpolished and broken.
defects.evidence: Text includes: '[VIDEO SCRIPT END] Sofi aprendió "escuela" y "maestra"... [VIDEO SCRIPT END]'
defects.fix: Sanitize and strip internal generation tags/metadata before delivering messages to the user interface.

result.best: Hyper-local, actionable guidance for navigating Panama institutions (CSS requirements and Fiestas Patrias November context).
result.why_pay_or_not: Calling me by the wrong name and leaking internal system code tags makes the service feel like an unreliable wrapper around an LLM rather than a secure, premium product worth paying for.

defects.what: The system repeatedly calls me by the wrong name.
defects.evidence: "Llegar desde Valencia ya es un paso enorme, Ana, y ya estás aquí." and "Good luck on Monday, Ana, you've got this."
defects.fix: Ensure the system pulls the correct user profile name (Carlos) rather than hallucinating or hardcoding 'Ana'.

defects.what: The bot translates nearly every sentence line-by-line into English, creating tedious, cluttered text instead of natural conversation or targeted English practice.
defects.evidence: Examples include: 'Significa en un rato, quizás hoy, quizás mañana... 😄 It means in a while, maybe today...', 'La pregunta que casi siempre abre una entrevista americana es "Tell me about yourself." La pregunta que casi siempre abre una entrevista americana es "Tell me about yourself."', and 'Estamos en noviembre, el mes de la patria. We're in November, the month of the homeland.'
defects.fix: Respond in Spanish for cultural settling advice, and offer English selectively for practical phrasing/interview practice rather than mirroring every single Spanish sentence.

result.best: The accurate Panamanian cultural context, specifically explaining what 'está chuleta' means when applied to work.
result.why_pay_or_not: Calling me by the wrong name twice and repeating every sentence in English shows broken state handling and unusable clutter.
